title: Piloting
text:
Mount Free Wave antenna outside on the rails of a boat as high as possible and connect cable to a Free Wave (RF) modem. Then, connect the serial port of the RF modem to a laptop running a terminal program (e.g., TeraTerm). Turn on and run the terminal software.
In TeraTerm, select Serial and then the correct COM Port.

If you want you can confirm the correct settings Setup -> Serial Port:. COM port: correct COM#. Baud rate: 115200. P-D-S: N-8-1, flow control - none.

Replace RED plug with GREEN plug in glider tail. Make sure that the glider tail with antenna is facing open skies and not obstructed by anything to get GPS from satellites. If you don’t see a readout in TeraTerm after inserting the Green plug, try connecting to another available COM port.
After the glider is powered up you should see glider status on the terminal window. Wait for the next lines:
:::{.border} > Sequencing missions  > load_mission(): Opening Mission file: initial.mi for execution once  > load_mission(): Opening Mission file: lastgasp.mi for execution FOREVER  > 1 mission specifiers - sequencing 1 total missions (not counting astgasp.mi):  > initial.mi  > lastgasp.mi :::
Record the vacuum, battery, and reset the ocean pressure.

CTRL C to interrupt this process and exit to GliderDOS.
put c_air_pump 0 command to release air from the air bladder.
callback 30 to stop glider from calling Iridium satellite for 30 minutes.
get m_vacuum to check vacuum and confirm that it is normal (6 +/-0.2 inHg). Could be higher if in a colder environment (close to 7).

If it is too low (not enough vacuum) the buoyancy pump may be in the wrong position; wait, re-read vacuum.
Record this value.

get m_battery; record the value.
zero_ocean_pressure to make sure run status.mi works properly

Enter “run status.mi” and wait for the message ‘MS_COMPLETED_NORMALLY (-1)’. Glider will get a GPS fix in the end, which you should confirm. Look for reports about vacuum, battery voltage, leak detect, and any abnormal messages.

callback 30
put c_air_pump 0
(optional) use

To check for installed devices in use on the glider


(Optional) Check the current “goto_l30.ma” for correct way points, “surfac30.ma”, and “yo30.ma” settings by using the “type” command. For example:
:::{.border} > cd mafiles  > type surfac30.ma         (look for 15 minutes as the active time) :::
Usually after status.mi is completed, the glider will inflate the air bladder. You will need to deflate it. Type:

put c_air_pump 0
exit
When you see a message saying that you can pull the GREEN plug, replace it with the RED one. Now you can leave the dock.

When you leave the dock, Call or Text the Pilot, and indicate you are leaving the dock.





Untie and set the glider on the vessel’s fantail, attach the wings. Make sure that laptop is on and terminal software (ProComm) is up and running on a laptop.
Replace RED plug with the GREEN plug in the glider tail.

Make sure that the glider tail with antenna is facing open skies and not abstracted by anything to get GPS from satellites.

After the glider is powered up you should see glider status on the terminal window. Wait for the next lines:

> Sequencing missions
> load_mission(): Opening Mission file: initial.mi for execution once
> load_mission(): Opening Mission file: lastgasp.mi for execution FOREVER
> 1 mission specifiers - sequencing 1 total missions (not counting astgasp.mi):
> initial.mi
> lastgasp.mi

Record the vacuum again.

CTRL C to interrupt this process and exit to GliderDOS.
put c_air_pump 0 command to release air from the air bladder.
callback 30 to stop glider from calling Iridium satellite for 30 minutes.
get m_vacuum to check vacuum and confirm that it is normal (6 +/-0.2 inHg). Could be higher if in a colder environment (close to 7).

If it is too low (not enough vacuum) the buoyancy pump may be in the wrong position; wait, re-read vacuum.
Record this value.


Enter “run status.mi” and wait for the message ‘MS_COMPLETED_NORMALLY (-1)’. Glider will get a GPS fix in the end, which you should confirm. Look for reports about vacuum, battery voltage, leak detect, and any abnormal messages.

Pilot may dockzr -archive -f irid * to send files from to-glider SFMC to glider
Pilot may dockszr -archive . to send file from to-science to glider
Pilot will callback 30 and confirm with field tech
use (e.g., ‘use + attitude_rev’)

If the status.mi mission is successful, the glider is ready for deployment.

DO NOT deflate the air bladder after status.mi on deck is completed. Air bladder must be inflated before the glider is deployed.

Deploy the glider.





When the glider is in the water, check for any suspicious pitch and roll. Glider’s tail must be reasonably sticking out above the water for Iridium, FreeWave, and GPS communications.
run status.mi and wait for the message ‘MS_COMPLETED_NORMALLY (-1)’. Glider will get a GPS fix in the end, which you should confirm. Look for any reports about vacuum, battery voltage, leak detect, and any abnormal messages.

callback 30
use

After confirming the status.mi is successful:

send .sbd .tbd (this will send files to local computer directory)
exit reset (to reboot the glider)
You should see glider status on the terminal window. Wait for the next lines:


> Sequencing missions
> load_mission(): Opening Mission file: initial.mi for execution once
> load_mission(): Opening Mission file: lastgasp.mi for execution FOREVER
> 1 mission specifiers - sequencing 1 total missions (not counting lastgasp.mi):
> initial.mi
> lastgasp.mi

Get fresh lat/lon.

CTRL C to interrupt this process and exit to GliderDOS
IMPORTANT! DO NOT deflate the air bladder and do not disable the Iridium.
callback 3 (to get fresh lat/lon)

Pilot will take over control of the glider. Pilot will let you know when the glider receives the mission command.

Pilot will loadmission waterclr.mi to clear depth averaged currents records
Pilot will run mission (ex. run vem_azfp.mi or sequence vem_azfp.mi(5), nhg2test.mi (5 to run mission 5 times)

Glider will start the mission. Keep the glider in sight and watch it dive. When glider dives report this to the pilot immediately since the pilot will be disconnected much earlier from the glider on the glider terminal over Iridium.
IMPORTANT! After glider dives and pilot was informed, TURN OFF the FreeWave modem.

If the FreeWave modem is still on, the glider will never call Iridium and connect to Dockerver.
Pilot: change script to driftsh.xml or vemaz_sh.xml once glider has disconnected

Deployment team must stick around for the first 15+ minutes to protect the glider when it surfaces for the first time. The pilot will call you back as soon as the glider is on the surface and data from the first 15 minutes of the mission are analyzed and the glider is sent for a longer period of surfacing time.
Go home.

title: Basestation
text:
Reprocess.py Reprocess.py starts with the .log and .eng files and can regenerate netcdf files, run Flight Model and generate plots.
Regenerate all netcdf files, run Flight Model and generate plots:

/opt/basestation/bin/python /usr/local/basestation3/Reprocess.py \
 --mission_dir <seaglider_home_directory> --force --reprocess_plots
Regenerate the dive 100 through 102 netcdf files, not re-running Flight Model
/opt/basestation/bin/python /usr/local/basestation3/Reprocess.py \
 --mission_dir <seaglider_home_directory> --force --skip_flight_model 100:102

BaseDB.py The mission database is added to during the normal logout processing. If there was ever a need to regenerate the database:
/opt/basestation/bin/python /usr/local/basestation3/BaseDB.py \
 --mission_dir <seaglider_home_directory> addncfs
BasePlot.py Any of the plots may be generated outside of the normal logout processing.
To generate all the plots for dive 100, generating stand-alone html files, in addition to the normal output:
/opt/basestation/bin/python /usr/local/basestation3/BasePlot.py \
 --mission_dir <seaglider_home_directory>  --plot_types dives --full_html p0010100.nc
To regenerate the whole mission plots:
/opt/basestation/bin/python /usr/local/basestation3/BasePlot.py \
 --mission_dir <seaglider_home_directory>  --plot_types mission
MoveData.py MoveData.py is used to clean up a Seaglider’s home directory prior to a new deployment.
/opt/basestation/bin/python /usr/local/basestation3/MoveData.py \
 --mission_dir <seaglider_home_directory> -t <target_directory> --verbose
BaseCtrlFiles.py BaseCtrlFiles.py contains the low-level routines that send notifications sent via the pagers.yml configuration files. For debugging purposes, these routines can be accessed directly, but they may not generate meaningful content. Additionally, it is possible to dump the merged pagers.yml dictionary.
To execute a low-level notification, simply supply one of the low-level notification tags:
/opt/basestation/bin/python /usr/local/basestation3/BaseCtrlFiles.py \
 --mission_dir <seaglider_home_directory> [--group_etc <group_etc_directory>] [divetar,upload,lategps,errors,drift,comp,tracebackrecov,alerts,gps,critical]
For example, gps will dispatch the GPS position found in the last comm session in the comm.log to those users subscribing to gps notifications.
To dump the merged pagers.yml dictionary:
/opt/basestation/bin/python /usr/local/basestation3/BaseCtrlFiles.py \
 --mission_dir <seaglider_home_directory> [--group_etc <group_etc_directory>] dump_pagers_yml
